nodes.title: shell.openPath is blocking on Linux when it should be non-blocking
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu, Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

shell.openPath should not be a blocking call.

### Actual Behavior

On Linux shell.openPath _is_ a blocking call.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Here is the linux implementation of shell.openPath (`shell/common/platform_util_linux.cc:349`)
```
void OpenPath(const base::FilePath& full_path, OpenCallback callback) {
  // This is async, so we don't care about the return value.
  XDGOpen(full_path.DirName(), full_path.value(), true, std::move(callback));
}
```
The third argument to `XDGOpen` is `true`. That argument is named `wait_for_exit` and causes the call to `XDGOpen` to be synchronous when true. (`XDGOpen` is defined on line 276 of the same file.)

That `true` should be `false`.

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

SteamOS 3.7.13 (Steam Deck)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

34.0.0

### Expected Behavior

Electron apps should start normally and the [Steam overlay](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/overlay) should function without issue.

### Actual Behavior

The Steam overlay briefly flashes and then disappears entirely. It remains disabled until a full system reboot.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Notes:**
I realize this may be a niche use case, so I understand if support is limited. However, I'd appreciate any guidance on what might be causing the issue. I'm happy to assist in tracking it down (I am a developer), though I'm not familiar with the Electron codebase. Are there any command-line flags I could try that might help? I'm open to testing and looking for any direction.

**Is this a Steam issue?**
That was my initial assumption. However, there were no Steam updates when the problem began. The issue started immediately after updating from Electron 34 to 35. Reverting to Electron 34 resolves it, and upgrading again reintroduces the bug.

**Relevance:**
Steam is a major platform, and many apps built with Electron integrate with it, so maintaining overlay compatibility could benefit a lot of developers.

### Problem Description

I want to show my electron app on a specific monitor that the user chooses. This should persist even after system restarts or unplugging and plugging them again in a different order. 



### Proposed Solution

Add the serial number of the monitor or the PnP device ID to the Display properties. This way we can easily identify the right monitor in any circumstance.

### Alternatives Considered

Currently, Display object in Electron has no properties that can be used for this. Screen sizes can be the same, screen position can be rearranged and id is unique but not persistent across system reboots.

### What operating system(s) are you using?

### Operating System Version

Darwin  23.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 23.6.0: Thu Mar  6 21:58:03 PST 2025; root:xnu-10063.141.1.704.6~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Given a fresh Electron application generated from the default template, and using `child_process.fork` in the main process, Electron should spawn the corresponding Helper as Node.js and execute the specified module both during development `npm run start` and in the generated application with `npm run make`.

The linked repository isolates the observed behavior:
https://github.com/kriskowal/electron-isolate-fork-defect/

```js
if (process.env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE) {
  console.error('unexpected');
  console.error(__filename);
  console.error(process.argv);
  console.error(process.env);
  return;
}
const { fork } = require('node:child_process');
const path = require('node:path');
fork(path.join(__dirname, 'child.js'), [], {});
```

For this program, I expect `npm run start` to behave the same as `npm run make && out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/MacOS/isolate-fork`. They should print out `expected` (as evidence that `child.js` executed).

### Actual Behavior

Running `npm run start` works as expected.

Running `npm run make && out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/MacOS/isolate-fork`, the application logs `unexpected` with the diagnostic information indicating that `fork` enters `main.js` instead of `child.js`.

```
unexpected
/Users/kris/isolate-electron/isolate-fork/out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/src/index.js
[
  '/Users/kris/isolate-electron/isolate-fork/out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/Frameworks/isolate-fork Helper.app/Contents/MacOS/isolate-fork Helper',
  '/Users/kris/isolate-electron/isolate-fork/out/isolate-fork-darwin-x64/isolate-fork.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/src/child.js'
]
{
  ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: '1',
.
.
.
```

https://github.com/kriskowal/electron-isolate-fork-defect/blob/main/src/index.js

### Expected Behavior

Long animation frames (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/long-animation-frames) should come with script attribution, making it easy to figure out which scripts are contributing to hitches in your application. If I take [this fiddle](https://gist.github.com/alexhaugland/498d878b7fff5a578c0ca6da03d836f8) and serve the index.html from python (`python3 -m http.server 9911` or similar) then I get nice console logs like this:
```json
obs1 {
    "name": "long-animation-frame",
    "entryType": "long-animation-frame",
    "startTime": 905.7000000476837,
    "duration": 250.964,
    "renderStart": 0,
    "styleAndLayoutStart": 0,
    "firstUIEventTimestamp": 0,
    "blockingDuration": 200.964,
    "scripts": [
        {
            "name": "script",
            "entryType": "script",
            "startTime": 905.8999998569489,
            "duration": 250,
            "invoker": "DOMWindow.onkeydown",
            "invokerType": "event-listener",
            "windowAttribution": "self",
            "executionStart": 905.8999998569489,
            "forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration": 0,
            "pauseDuration": 0,
            "sourceURL": "http://localhost:9911/",
            "sourceFunctionName": "block",
            "sourceCharPosition": 19
        }
    ]
}
```

The script attribution here makes it easy to figure out which script is causing the stuttering. The specific code in the fiddle was adopted from https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals/blob/8a54167b8a455128bd5ae0f3729c3e81ea146f62/test/views/inp.njk. 

### Actual Behavior

When loading the [above fiddle](https://gist.github.com/alexhaugland/498d878b7fff5a578c0ca6da03d836f8) I do not observe the same behavior. The events look more like:
```json

    "startTime": 2289.7000000476837,
    "duration": 151.39999985694885,

    "styleAndLayoutStart": 2441.0999999046326,
    "firstUIEventTimestamp": 2287.7999999523163,

}

obs2 {

    "styleAndLayoutStart": 2441.0999999046326,
    "firstUIEventTimestamp": 2287.7999999523163,

} 
```
and contain no script attribution at all. I see similar behavior if I load the `index.html` as a `file://` url which could be related.

### Expected Behavior

Toggling system settings for titlebar and window accent color should be reflected without having to restart the application

### Actual Behavior

Application needs to be restarted to respect the system settings

### Testcase Gist URL

### Additional Information

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')

function createWindow () {
  const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    frame: false,
    titleBarOverlay: true,
  })

  mainWindow.loadFile('index.html')
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  createWindow()
})

app.on('window-all-closed', function () {
  if (process.platform !== 'darwin') app.quit()
})
```



* Run the application
* Enable `Show accent colors on title bars and window borders` setting
* Application gets accent border
* Disable the system setting
* See that the border is not removed, requires an application restart
